source_title: Best Save Ideas for Football Manager 27
source_excerpt:
As is the case in all installments of the franchise, the hardest decision when loading Football Manager 2027 for the first time is choosing a team to manage. With dozens of countries and leagues to pick between and hundreds of teams, ranging from non-league outfits to continental champions, the choice can be an overwhelming one. Of course, one option is to start off unemployed and see which teams let their managers go, but for those looking to lead a club from the get-go, the following are some interesting save ideas for FM 27 . These teams could be perfect for rags-to-riches playthroughs, in need of a rebuild, or in unique circumstances making for memorable careers.
The Champions From 10 Years Ago Have Fallen To League One
League: League One (English 3rd Tier)
Just a decade ago, Leicester stunned the sporting world by winning the Premier League as 5000/1 underdogs. However, after a calamitous double relegation, they now find themselves floundering in League One with a bloated wage bill and a tonne of work to make it back to the top flight. This makes for a perfect Football Manager 27 save, with players able to rebuild and take Leicester on a journey that has the potential to surpass the club's exploits under Claudio Ranieri.
Down In The Third Tier For The First Time
League: Primera Federacion Group 2 (Spanish 3rd Tier)
After a decade in the second tier of Spanish football, but having spent the majority of their time in the top flight, Real Zaragoza have fallen into the third tier for the first time in the club's history. As one of the most supported clubs in Spain, Zaragoza have plenty of potential, but they need life breathing into them, arguably starting with a complete rebuild and new identity on the pitch. One day, you could aim for a league title with The Aragonese, which would represent a first, although they have won a few Copa del Reys.
Instantly Return To The Prem & Make A Splash
League: Championship (English 2nd Tier)
West Ham United were Conference League winners in 2023, and despite fighting to the last day of last season, they have fallen to the second tier of English football for the first time since 2012. With a huge stadium and a squad still full of talent, including club captain Jared Bowen, himself a Football Manager fan, prospective managers have plenty of potential in front of them. Naturally, the aim is immediate promotion, but from there a fresh start and rebuilt ethos could see West Ham make a triumphant return.
A Non-League Club With Taskmaster Links
League: National League South (English 6th Tier)
Fans of the hit comedy TV show Taskmaster might recognize the name Chesham United, as a few tasks have taken place at their ground, and one even involved the club's mascot. Furthermore, the team is sponsored by Taskmaster, and the star/creator of the show, Alex Horne, is a director of Chesham United, even appearing as a member of staff in Football Manager ​. The fact that Chesham are a 6th tier side makes them a perfect candidate for a rags-to-riches playthrough, but with the added panache of their comedy partner. As a manager, you could aim to entertain on and off the pitch while signing players known for their humor as well as their footballing prowess.
Raid The Champions League With Viking FK
League: Eliteserien (Norwegian 1st Tier)
After the success of Bodo/Glimt in last season's Champions League, the Norwegian Eliteserien is on the rise, with national champions Viking FK making the League Phase this time out. The aim is to keep winning and improving the quality of the Norwegian league, while attempting to make a historic run in Europe worthy of the club's imposing name. You could even try to develop young Norwegian talent to play alongside the likes of Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard and one day lead the national team to international glory.
League: Premier League (English 1st Tier)
Everton are near the top of the English Misery table, which tracks how long it's been since a team last won a title, cup, or promotion, with their last silverware being the 1995 FA Cup. While this is slightly misleading, as Everton finished in European spots multiple times over the last two decades, there's still no denying that 31 years is a long time without anything to truly celebrate. After a few years of turbulence and close shaves with relegation, Everton have a brand-new stadium, a young, hungry squad, and some life back. This could be the perfect time to take the reins and win any trophy with the Merseyside club.
The Newest Red Bull Team In Japan With Connected Talent Pools
League: J2 League (Japanese 2nd Tier)
While the Red Bull conglomerate of football teams might not be popular with all, there's no denying that they produce fantastic talent and play exciting football. RB Omiya Ardija is the newest addition to the franchise, and Japan may be a nation or even continent where players haven't managed previously. Situated in the second tier, where they have spent most of the past decade, the aim is to take Omiya to the next level, while developing young Japanese talents that may be fed to teams such as RB Leipzig or RB Salzburg, and into the national team. All these clubs are connected in-game, so you can expect unique interactions, making for a memorable save.
Return This Historic Club To The Top Of Scottish Football
League: William Hill League 2 (Scottish 4th Tier)
After Rangers won the inaugural Scottish title, Dumbarton followed this up with back-to-back wins in 1891 and 1892, but have not played in the top flight since 1985, finding themselves all the way down in 21st on the all-time points tally for the division. Having bounced around the three lower tiers ever since, Dumbarton now find themselves in League Two with a long, long journey back to reclaim their history. This is not a save for the faint-hearted, as only a maximum of two teams can gain promotion, with a club from the tier above joining the playoffs. Nevertheless, the small leagues in Scotland are more intimate and have a unique setup, making for memorable careers.
More Teams To Manage In Football Manager 27
The following are more options for your FM 27 saves, with some clubs being in similar circumstances to those above, and others being interesting in their own right.
Scunthorpe: A non-league club that was in the League One playoffs as recently as 2018.
Carlisle: Looking to get back to the Football League with plenty of money.
Morecambe: A former League Two staple in free-fall after financial trouble.
Forest Green: Revitalize this eco-friendly club.
York City: A return to the Football League with a historic city.
Fleetwood: Follow-up on their League Cup shock against Arsenal.
Wigan Athletic: A former Prem side on the brink of dropping to League Two.
Hearts: Win the title after last season's heartbreak.
St. Pauli: An exciting team that took a hit last season.
Wolfsburg: Former Bundesliga champions looking to bounce back from relegation.
SV Elversberg: A young promoted team from a small town making shock waves across Germany.
Vitesse Arnhem: First-tier Dutch staples fallen for the first time in decades.
FC Nantes: A solid French side struggling in the second division.
Montpellier HSC: The surprise champions of 2012 back in the second tier.
UC Sampdoria: Champions in the early 90s, unable to get out of Serie B.
